With less than 11 days until the midterm elections, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton brought his statewide campaign to Laredo on Friday afternoon, holding a get-out-the-vote event at the Palenque Grill off San Bernardo Avenue and I-35, according to KGNS.

The Laredo stop was one of 12 on Paxton's “Come and Take It Tour” this election season, the station reported. Paxton laid out an economic vision he calls the “Protecting the Texas Promise Plan,” which includes tax deductions for home down payments and out-of-pocket medical expenses, doubling the child tax credit, “healthy living” deductions covering nutrition plans, GLP-1 medication, and gym memberships, and making Trump accounts permanent.

Paxton also drew a sharp contrast with his opponent, state Rep. James Talarico, calling him the most radical Democrat ever to run for statewide office, according to KGNS.

Supporters in the room said they left energized. Marta Loera, a retired teacher, said she attended because she is conservative and believes Paxton stands for her beliefs. Dolores Medrano, a retired educator, said the event fired up supporters to keep campaigning — holding signs and calling voters — adding that there is a lot at stake in Laredo.

KGNS also reported that Talarico is expected to appear in Laredo on Sunday, Oct. 25. Early voting in Texas runs through Oct. 30, and Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Sources: KGNS, reporting by Luis Enrique Vela, Oct. 23, 2026.

title: Paxton brings 'Come and Take It' tour to Laredo, pitches economic plan 11 days before midterms
